henry.title: Moon and Mars: Predict the Sky, Then Look
henry.intro: About 15 minutes after the grown-up says go. You will predict, look, and separate a NASA fact from a game picture. Write question 1 before you open Show me how. The picture can spoil the prediction.
setup: This page cannot start Regolith. On the Windows PC, open moonsim.exe yourself. There is no launch button on purpose.

This candidate is b1505a7. It had a short window check only. It was not drive-tested, and this lesson was not tested on your PC. Later fixes may not be in the file. Press H and follow Help if it disagrees with this page.
Keep any career you want. Do not overwrite it. Backspace recovery may cost something. Do not hand Backspace to Henry.
Confirm in H, then use Load or a new career and garage/drive until a world is showing. Henry’s keys are W A S D. You handle menus (Esc, the map button or Shift+M, Tab). Trust H.

Two landings today: a readable Moon name first (Moon menu titles were not verified — write the name you actually see), then Mars. Prefer Gale crater (Curiosity / Mount Sharp) if it is readable. Other readable Mars names: Jezero crater, Meridiani Planum, Olympus Mons, Valles Marineris, Chasma Boreale. The map click was not retested. Pause the 15 minutes while you switch.

Do not use Titan, Io, or Europa. Skip a site with no readable name. Ignore a little globe if it flickers or disagrees with the ground. Do not rank worlds by speed or jumps. There is no verified gravity or air gauge.
If a world will not appear, Henry uses the older-build photos on this page plus the NASA pages and writes BACKUP. Those photos are not today’s screen. The game is still the plan when it runs.
steps: 📖 Read three short chunks. Answer the checks.
✏️ Write question 1 before anyone opens the game view or Show me how.
👀 Look at the Moon, then Mars. W moves, A and D turn, S backs up. Stop and write.
🧠 Finish the worksheet: prediction, what you saw, and the NASA numbers.
links: NASA Space Place: All About the Moon
Grown-up check only. The reading already has the sentence. You do not read the whole page.
NASA Space Place: All About Mars
Find the idea: Mars has a very thin atmosphere, mostly carbon dioxide, and rusty ground.
Surface gravity 1.62 m/s². The atmosphere is only a trace.
Surface gravity 3.73 m/s². Surface pressure about 6.36 millibars. Mostly carbon dioxide.

passage.text: 🌕 An older game view of the Moon showed grey craters, a black sky, and sharp shadows. An older Gale view of Mars showed rusty ground and a tan horizon. Those are reminders, not orders. You will write what today’s screen shows.
passage.a: What I see today, not a promise from an old picture.

passage.text: 📖 NASA lists the Moon’s pull as 1.62 m/s² and Mars as 3.73 m/s². Mars has thin carbon-dioxide air. The Moon’s air is only a trace. The game model is close to those pulls, but this screen has no gauge. You do not measure them.
passage.q: Are 1.62 and 3.73 numbers you measure with the rover today?
passage.a: No. They are NASA fact-sheet numbers. The game model is close, but it is not a gauge reading.

passage.text: 🌫️ Thin air can color a sky. Almost no air can leave a sky looking black. Predict before you look. Brightness and color in the game are approximations. A dark picture can be the lighting, not a proof about air. Do not compare driving speeds. Little rocks are model scenery, not a lab sample.
passage.q: What can fool your eyes besides the real air?
passage.a: Brightness or exposure — how light or dark the picture is made.

words: the layer of gases around a world
the line where ground meets sky
a number or picture built to stand in for the real thing
how bright or dark the picture is
a round pit; on a real world, often from an impact

handsOn.title: After question 1 is written: Moon, then Mars
steps: guides/draw-adult.svg
Grown-up. Confirm H. Open a readable Moon name. Write that name on the sheet. Henry does not open Windows.
guides/draw-wasd.svg
Henry. Roll a short way with W. Turn with A and D. Stop. Write the sky and the ground. Do not use speed as science.
guides/draw-adult.svg
Grown-up. Pause the timer. Switch to a readable Mars place, Gale if you can read it. Henry looks again and writes.
guides/moon-old-example.png
After both looks. This is a real older-build Moon photo: grey craters, black sky, sharp shadow. It is not today’s screen and not the controls.
guides/mars-old-example.png
This is a real older-build Gale photo: rusty ground, tan horizon. Say what matches today and what does not. Small rocks are model scenery.
handsOn.look: A black or colored sky, rusty or grey ground, round pits, shadows. Sky color does not prove the air. Missing a famous landmark is allowed.

worksheet:
Before you look. I predict the more colored or hazy sky is: Moon / Mars.
Because: ________________________________

What I saw. Moon name: ________ Sky: ________ Ground: ________
Mars name: ________ Sky: ________ Ground: ________
Source: GAME or BACKUP

Compare. My prediction matched / did not match.
One thing besides air that can change the picture: ________________

NASA, not a gauge. Moon ________ m/s²   Mars ________ m/s²
I did not measure these. Little rocks in the game are model scenery. Circle: true / false
henry.challenge: Optional. If H and the HUD show a speed, copy the number and the unit and label it SCREEN. Do not use it to answer 1–4. A changing speed means a distance guess is not a measured trip. Do not compare top speed on two worlds.

parentKey.assess: Score the worksheet only. Reading checks are support. 5 = a prediction with a reason about air, real look-notes for both worlds (or a labeled BACKUP), a confound that is brightness/exposure/color approximation, and the NASA gravities labeled as not measured. Do not require the old picture’s exact colors if the live view differs. Do not require a speed.
parentKey.limits: No drive validation of b1505a7. No verified E, M, Home, Shift-boost, or Space-jump. No jump test and no cross-world speed test. Globe is not evidence. Gravity and pressure are references, not instruments. Moon model about 1.62 m/s² and no air; Mars model about 3.7 m/s² and about 610 Pa of thin CO2. NASA fact sheet is the real-world source: Moon 1.62 m/s²; Mars 3.73 m/s² and about 6.36 millibars, mostly CO2. The lesson photos are older-build appearance examples only (grey cratered Moon, black sky, sharp shadow; rusty Gale ground, tan horizon), not the current screen and not control evidence. Scarps, rays, jets, and ice are not required. Titan, Io, and Europa are out.

items.a: The strongest prediction is Mars, because NASA says it has a thin atmosphere and the Moon has only a trace of air. Credit a clear reason tied to air. A Moon prediction can still earn credit if the reason is thoughtful and question 3 deals honestly with the result.

Any specific sky and ground notes, with the names actually opened. Older-build reminders, not required words: Moon black sky, grey craters, sharp shadows; Mars rusty ground, tan horizon. Live view may differ. BACKUP is valid if the game failed: the older-build photos plus Space Place, labeled BACKUP.
Must name something like brightness, exposure, or that game color is an approximation. Not speed, not jump height, not “the globe said so.”

Moon 1.62 m/s² and Mars 3.73 m/s² from the NASA fact sheets. Circle true: little rocks are model scenery. The game model’s 3.7 m/s² and about 610 Pa are close references, not what he measures and not a substitute for 3.73 and 6.36 millibars.

frankie.title: Two Worlds to Look At 🌕🔴
frankie.intro: Grown-up, read aloud. We look at the Moon, then Mars. Frankie picks what he sees. About 14 minutes after you say go. Setup time is yours, not his.
setup: Open Regolith yourself. This page cannot launch it. Press H and confirm keys before he drives. His keys are W A S D only.
Candidate b1505a7 was not drive-tested. Follow H if it disagrees with this page. Do not overwrite a save you want. Do not give him Backspace.
Land a readable Moon name, then a readable Mars name (Gale crater if you can read it). Pause his minutes while you switch. Skip Titan, Io, Europa, and any nameless site.
If the game will not show a world, let him point at the older-build photos on this page. He writes BACKUP. Those photos are not today’s screen. The game is still the plan when it runs.
steps: 👀 Look at the Moon. Point to 1, 2, or 3 things.
🔤 Copy a word that matches. Other is allowed.
👀 Look at Mars. Point again. Same or different?
✏️ Trace I see it. Write your word if you can.
links: NASA Space Place: All About the Moon
Grown-up: show a Moon picture if the game is down.

handsOn.title: Look, point, count your own points
steps: guides/draw-wasd.svg
Hold W a little. Stop. A and D turn. S backs up. Grown-up already opened the Moon.
guides/card-count.svg
Point to things YOU see. Count only your points. 0, 1, 2, or 3 can be right.
guides/moon-old-example.png
Older-build Moon photo. Not today’s screen and not the buttons. Point only if it matches what you see.
guides/mars-old-example.png
Older-build Mars photo. Rusty ground, tan horizon. After Mars is open, say same or different.
guides/draw-adult.svg
Grown-up. You switch worlds. He does not use the menus.
handsOn.look: A light place, a dark place, a round mark, or the sky. His count does not have to match yours.
handsOn.q: Count, copy a word, and say same or different.

worksheet:
Moon. I pointed to this many things (0, 1, 2, or 3): ______
Word that matches what I saw: gray   dark   other ______

Mars. I pointed to this many things: ______
Word that matches: red   tan   other ______

Sound it out. Draw a line.
red   sun   hop
🐇   ☀️   🔴
Circle every see: I see the sky. I see it.

Trace: I see it.
Stretch: Write the word you copied:

parentKey.assess: Score the looking, not a secret crater total. Any count 0–3 is right if it matches what he pointed to. The copied word must match his choice, including other. Same/different should match his two looks. Word match: red-circle, sun-sun, hop-rabbit. Both see words circled. Stretch spelling is extra.
parentKey.limits: Same build limits as Henry. Do not require three features. Do not require the word red. No drawing. No jump test.

items.a: Accept his count. Gray or dark fits a typical Moon view; red or tan fits a typical Mars view; other is correct when the screen disagrees. Same/different is his comparison.
red → 🔴, sun → ☀️, hop → 🐇. Circle both see. Trace “I see it.”
